top_stories.title: Binance Hit by Record $6.3B Hack, Attributed to North Korea, Then Reopens Withdrawals
points: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, suffered a breach of roughly $6.3-6.4 billion, the largest crypto heist on record
FBI and blockchain investigators (TRM, Chainalysis) attributed the theft to North Korea's state-linked TraderTraitor hacking group
Withdrawals were halted after the attack but reopened within days, signaling the exchange had stabilized operations
Despite reopening, $3.6 billion (about 2.1% of total assets) exited within the first 9.5 hours, showing significant customer exodus
Analyst Tom Lee argued the relatively 'muted' market response proves growing industry resilience; his firm Bitmine bought $19 million more Ethereum during the chaos

unique_angles.point: Bitcoin ETFs saw $643 million in outflows on Friday alone (October's largest single-day outflow), though Bitcoin's price only dropped 1.3% from the shock
Ethereum prediction markets show a near-even split: 51% betting on a crash to $1,500 vs 49% expecting a rally to $3,000, both about 33% away from the current $2,253 price
Frames the breach and swift recovery as underscoring systemic risks in centralized exchange custody and trading infrastructure

top_stories.title: Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Transfers After Separate Security Incident
points: Brazil's largest exchange, Mercado Bitcoin, halted all deposits and withdrawals following a security compromise
The exchange lost an estimated $40 million in the exploit
Tether (issuer of the USDT stablecoin, a cryptocurrency pegged to the US dollar) froze over 4.5 million USDT linked to the theft
The incident, coming days after the Binance hack, compounds concerns about security standards across the exchange industry and creates liquidity problems for affected users

unique_angles.point: Open-source Bitcoin payment tool BTCPay Server separately ordered all operators to shut down servers after attackers targeted hot wallets (internet-connected crypto storage) running outdated software

items.title: Major Companies Object to Tokenized Stock Trading Plans
points: 12 major companies, including Nvidia and Nike, objected to having their shares tokenized (converted into blockchain-based digital tokens representing stock ownership) on a planned crypto trading venue
U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday flagged as the next potential catalyst for crypto market moves
